# Tovuk agent guide

Tovuk deploys Rust workers, static frontends, and worker-static services.
Worker-static services use one root tovuk.toml, serve the frontend at `/`, and route
`/api/*` to the Rust worker.

Use the native CLI after installing it with npm, Homebrew, PyPI, or Cargo:

```sh
tovuk check --json
tovuk deploy --dry-run --json
tovuk deploy --wait --json
```

Reference: [Tovuk docs](https://docs.tovuk.com).

Agent repair loop:

1. Run `tovuk check --json`.
2. If it fails, read the first failed check.
3. Apply its `agent_instruction` exactly.
4. Rerun check until it passes.
5. Run `tovuk deploy --dry-run --json`.
6. Review warnings, enabled and disabled capabilities, meters, limits, and
   `billingEstimate`.
7. Set hard usage caps for expected load.
8. Run `tovuk deploy --wait --json`.
9. If deploy fails, read `build_job.id` or the failed build id.
10. Run `tovuk logs --build <build_id> --json`.
11. Fix the first actionable log error.
12. Rerun `tovuk check --json` and `tovuk deploy --dry-run --json`.

Rust worker contract:

- `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`, and `tovuk.toml` are committed.
- `kind = "rust_worker"` is set in `tovuk.toml`.
- `[capabilities]` explicitly sets `worker = true`,
  `static_frontend = false`, platform capabilities to true, and unused optional
  resources to false.
- `[build].check` includes `cargo fmt --all --check`.
- `[build].check` includes release-mode
  `cargo check --locked --release --all-targets --all-features`.
- `[build].check` includes release-mode
  `cargo test --locked --release --all-targets --all-features`.
- `[build].check` includes
  `cargo clippy --locked --release --all-targets --all-features` with
  `-D warnings`, `-D clippy::all`, `-D clippy::pedantic`, panic/unwrap bans,
  and resource lints such as `large_futures`, `large_stack_frames`,
  `mem_forget`, and `redundant_clone`.
- `[resources].memory` is `128mb`.
- `[resources].cpu` is `1`; set `worker_cpu_ms` usage caps for CPU budget.
- `[resources].idle_timeout_minutes` stays between `1` and `60`.
- The server listens on `0.0.0.0:$PORT`.
- The configured health path returns HTTP 200.
- Direct `unsafe` is not allowed in workspace source.

Static frontend contract:

- `kind = "static_frontend"` is set in `tovuk.toml`.
- `[capabilities]` explicitly sets `static_frontend = true`,
  `worker = false`, platform capabilities to true, and unused optional
  resources to false.
- `package.json` is committed.
- A package lockfile is committed.
- Browser source is `.ts` or `.tsx` under `src`, `app`, `pages`, `routes`, or
  `components`.
- `package.json` has `typecheck`, `lint`, and `build` scripts.
- `typecheck` runs stable native type-aware TypeScript checks such as
  `oxlint --type-aware --type-check`.
- `lint` runs native tooling such as `oxlint`, `biome check`, or `deno lint`.
- `lint` also runs Fallow `dead-code`, semantic `dupes`, and `health` gates.
- `[build].check` installs dependencies and runs package scripts for typecheck
  and lint.
- Weak typecheck, fake lint, missing Fallow quality gates, and JavaScript-based
  lint/format scripts are rejected for deploys.
- JavaScript and TypeScript are frontend-only. API routes, SSR handlers,
  middleware, and server logic must move to the Rust worker.

Worker-static contract:

- One root `tovuk.toml` sets `kind = "worker_static"`.
- `[capabilities]` explicitly sets `static_frontend = true`, `worker = true`,
  platform capabilities to true, and unused optional resources to false.
- `[worker].root` points to the Rust worker.
- `[frontend].root` points to the static frontend.
- The frontend calls same-origin `/api`.
- The worker health path is `/api/healthz`.
- Worker build and runtime commands must use `cargo build --release` and a
  `./target/release/*` Rust binary, never Node, Bun, Deno, or TS runtimes.
- Queue handlers are Rust worker routes at `POST /.tovuk/queues/<queue>`.
- Queue batch size, batch timeout, retries, retention, and dead-letter routing
  are configurable through the CLI/API.
- Queue handler payloads contain base64 message bodies. Return `2xx` only after
  the batch is safely handled.
- Cron handlers are Rust worker routes at `POST /.tovuk/cron/<trigger>`.
- Cron handlers must be idempotent because schedules can overlap with retries
  or manual agent actions.
- WebSocket upgrades on worker routes are proxied to Rust workers and meter
  response-side tunnel bytes as `worker_transfer_bytes`.

Useful commands:

```sh
tovuk pricing --json
tovuk deploy --dry-run --json
curl https://api.tovuk.com/v1/status
tovuk usage --json
tovuk service list --json
tovuk service show <service> --json
tovuk service delete <service> --json
tovuk logs --build <build_id> --json
tovuk logs --service <service> --json
tovuk env list --service <service> --json
tovuk domains list --service <service> --json
tovuk database create --service <service> DB --json
tovuk database query --service <service> DB "select 1" --json
tovuk database backup create --service <service> DB --json
tovuk database backup list --service <service> DB --json
tovuk database backup restore --service <service> DB sqlite_backup_1 --json
tovuk database delete --service <service> DB --json
tovuk kv create --service <service> CACHE --json
tovuk kv namespace delete --service <service> CACHE --json
tovuk queue create --service <service> failed_jobs --json
tovuk queue create --service <service> jobs --max-batch-size 10 --max-batch-timeout-seconds 5 --dead-letter-queue failed_jobs --json
tovuk queue update --service <service> jobs --max-batch-size 25 --json
tovuk queue update --service <service> jobs --clear-dead-letter-queue --json
tovuk queue delete --service <service> jobs --json
tovuk cron create --service <service> nightly "0 0 * * *" --json
tovuk cron delete --service <service> nightly --json
tovuk state create --service <service> Room --json
tovuk state objects --service <service> Room --json
tovuk state keys --service <service> Room room-1 --json
tovuk state put --service <service> Room room-1 counter 1 --json
tovuk state get --service <service> Room room-1 counter --json
tovuk state alarm set --service <service> Room room-1 --delay-seconds 60 --json
tovuk state alarm get --service <service> Room room-1 --json
tovuk state alarm delete --service <service> Room room-1 --json
tovuk state delete --service <service> Room --json
tovuk binding create --service <service> AUTH_SERVICE --target auth-service --json
tovuk binding delete --service <service> AUTH_SERVICE --json
tovuk limits set worker_requests --period day --value 100000 --json
tovuk limits set state_requests --period month --value 1000000 --json
tovuk limits set state_sqlite_rows_written --period month --value 50000000 --json
tovuk limits delete worker_requests --period day --json
tovuk storage list --service <service> --json
tovuk storage upload --service <service> ./file.png uploads/file.png --public --json
tovuk storage download --service <service> uploads/file.png ./file.png --json
tovuk storage url --service <service> uploads/file.png --json
tovuk storage delete --service <service> uploads/file.png --json
tovuk billing checkout --json
tovuk support list --json
tovuk support create "Deploy failed" "Agent retried deploy after check." --service <service> --build <build_id> --deploy <deploy_id> --failing-command "tovuk deploy --wait --json" --first-log-line "first actionable log line" --json
tovuk support resolve <ticket_id> --json
tovuk abuse report https://demo.tovuk.app "Phishing page" "Credential collection form" --category phishing --reporter-email reporter@example.com --evidence "Screenshot URL and request id" --json
tovuk abuse list --json
tovuk abuse appeal abuse_0123456789abcdef0123 "Removed the reported file and rotated credentials." --evidence "deploy_1 remediation log" --json
```

`tovuk storage upload` automatically switches to multipart transfer for files
larger than 100 MiB. Object storage limits expose object size, part count,
metadata size, custom domains per storage bucket, bucket management operations,
and same-key write throughput.

Before load tests, production launch, or paid usage, run
`tovuk pricing --json` and set hard usage caps with `tovuk limits set`.
Useful cap metrics include `build_minutes`, `worker_requests`, `worker_cpu_ms`,
`sqlite_rows_read`, `sqlite_rows_written`, `kv_reads`, `queue_operations`,
`state_requests`, `state_duration_gb_milliseconds`, `state_sqlite_rows_read`,
`state_sqlite_rows_written`,
`object_storage_bytes`, `object_storage_class_a_operations`, and
`object_storage_class_b_operations`, and `object_storage_egress_bytes`.

`tovuk pricing --json` and `tovuk pricing --json` expose a
`products` catalog. Use each product's `features`, `meters`, `meter_details`,
`pricing_fields`, and `limit_fields` before load tests, media uploads, or paid
usage.
`tovuk deploy --dry-run --json` is read-only and combines `tovuk.toml`, quality checks,
capability meters, account limits, usage, and `billingEstimate` before deploy.
The catalog includes Worker, Static Frontend, SQLite, Object Storage, State,
KV, Queues, Cron, Service Bindings, Secrets, Custom Domains, Logs, Builds, and
Usage Caps.

Use `GET /v1/status` only when Tovuk itself appears unavailable. If the API is
available and a deploy fails, inspect build logs instead of changing status
checks.

Never print or commit secrets. Put secrets in Tovuk env vars with
`tovuk env set --service <service> KEY=value`.

When a free-tier limit blocks work, run `tovuk billing checkout --json` and
show the returned URL to the human. When Tovuk support is needed, create a
ticket only after collecting the failing command, service id, build id, deploy id,
first actionable log line, and what the agent already tried. Resolve the ticket
when the issue is fixed so future agents do not duplicate the same support
work.
